title: Where do you even publish an Al game?
author: OddMaintenance6305
selftext:
Saw someone asking this the other day. They made a game with Al tools and didn't know where to post it.

Tried Websim. Felt like it was more for websites.

Rosebud was closer. Still not quite right.

Someone in the replies mentioned Astrocade. Got me thinking though. A spot just for Al stuff? That actually sounds kind of nice. You wouldn't have to explain every weird texture. or spend half the comments defending the tool instead of talking about the game itself.

Then I was looking at Yoroll. They've got these feeds for interactive stories and small games. but I have no idea who's actually browsing them.

who's actually on the other end of those feeds? Like, are normal players browsing this stuff? Or is it mostly just creators checking out each other's projects?

If I'm being think I'd want both. Somewhere low pressure to throw the first rough version up. Somewhere people already know it's Al and won't make a big deal out of it. And then a second place where the game has to sink or swim on its own. No context, no caveats. Just whether it's actually fun. What about you?

comments.author: CubeUnleashed
comments.body: I never heard of these platforms, I just publish on steam. It has the largest userbase and a lot of tools for marketing.

replies.author: Livid_Shallot5701
replies.body: Yeah but he wants to complicate things needlessly

replies.author: Felwyin
replies.body: He doesn't want to publish, he wants to become a publisher.

replies.author: Strict-Broccoli-8877
replies.body: When the project is at a point where you don't want to explain weird textures to people, then it's probably not quite ready for steam and general audiences.

replies.author: astanar
replies.body: People dont want to pay the sign up fee because 99% know their game is crap

comments.author: ObviousPin2271
comments.body:
"AI" adds no value to games. It's a tool to make stuff.

"Where do i publish javascript games?! where i publish python games?"

They are just games.

Most people don't care. just publish it.

comments.author: StoneCypher
comments.body:
games go on steam.  why are you putting your games on random websites nobody has ever heard of?

put them on itch instead of steam if it's your first time and you need a practice run.

comments.author: Brewgazer
comments.body: Itch.io, I made a website for browser based ones called flashvibegames.com but I think I’m getting ready to change it to be utilized for game jams

comments.author: ivyentre
comments.body:
Put them wherever you put any game.

You have to understand a lot of AI hate is performative. AI games are like OnlyFans; everyone claims to hate them and wail about how bad it is for society, but someone must be buying it.

comments.author: Salty_Country6835
comments.body:
I think both is the right answer. An AI friendly space makes sense as a workshop where you can throw up rough builds and actually talk about the damn game instead of defending the existence of the tools for 40 comments.

But I wouldnt want that to become a bubble either. Eventually toss it onto itch, Steam, wherever normal players are. No caveats, no ideological cage match. Does the game work? Is it interesting? Is it fun?

Workshop first. Wild second.
